A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that a simple, yet powerful neural network architecture, trained end-to-end, is able to outperform previous methods in scene text recognition.
, we are the first to achieve state-of-the-art text recognition results without any hand-engineered features.
, we have shown that a simple end-to-end text recogniser can achieve comparable performance to state-of-the-art methods, while being much simpler to implement and train.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, with the right combination of neural network architectures and unsupervised feature representations, we can achieve highly accurate scene text recognition with a single end-to-end system that does not rely on hand-engineered features.
, in many computer vision problems, a combination of deep learning, unsupervised feature-learning and simple, off-the-shelf techniques is often enough to obtain state-of-the-art results.

, by leveraging the power of deep neural networks, we can achieve highly competitive text recognition performance with a very simple system that is easy to implement and train, and that does not rely on any hand-engineered features, nor on any large-scale training datasets.
